exposure: Analgesia during labor (pharmacologic and non-pharmacologic methods)
Upright positioning in the first stage of labor
Neuraxial anesthesia (epidural, spinal, combined spinal-epidural, dural puncture epidural)
Subcutaneous wound infiltration with local anesthetic
Individual patient priorities for labor pain management
outcome: Patient's sense of empowerment and control
Length of the second stage of labor
cohort: Patients experiencing labor who require pain management, including those with opioid use disorder.
finding: A patient's sense of empowerment and control, largely influenced by labor analgesia, is the most predictive factor for maternal satisfaction with childbirth, and various pharmacologic and non-pharmacologic methods offer effective pain relief with differing impacts on outcomes.
mod_finding: Neuraxial regional anesthesia is not associated with increased rates of cesarean delivery or assisted vaginal delivery, and it has only a small effect on the length of the second stage of labor.
country: N/A (The review discusses practices and statistics relevant to the United States).
